facts.big: The report has to be ready
facts.label: Prazos e tarefas
facts.sub: Use has/have to be + particípio para dizer o que precisa ser feito. Use by para o prazo. A forma negativa é don’t/doesn’t have to be.

facts.label: Tem que ser / estar
facts.sub: Use has/have to be + particípio para dizer o que precisa ser feito: The report has to be ready. Use has com singular e have com plural: The files have to be saved.

facts.label: Não precisa ser
facts.sub: Use don’t/doesn’t have to be + particípio quando não é necessário: It doesn’t have to be printed. Não significa proibido.

items.s: The report has to be finished by Friday.

items.s: Don’t have to be printed means it is forbidden.
items.why: It means it is not necessary.

answers: The report has to be finished by Friday. → Verdadeiro (Passive with have to.)
We say The report has to finished. → Falso (You need be: has to be finished.)
Don’t have to be printed means it is forbidden. → Falso (It means it is not necessary.)

pages.title: A busy office in Miami · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Wednesday afternoon in Miami. Zoe and Eli work in a busy office. The air conditioner is loud. A big report is almost ready. The customer wants it very soon. They check the list of tasks.

“Zoe, the report has to be ready by Friday. Is it finished?” says Eli. “Not yet. The numbers have to be checked first, and the charts have to be added.” says Zoe. “Who checks the numbers? They have to be checked by two people.” says Eli.
